articles.title: GPU Cluster Troubleshooting Guide for 2027: Isolating Originating Ranks in NCCL Timeouts and NVIDIA Xid Faults
articles.excerpt: Quick Answer: Never restart a crashed multi-node GPU job solely from a rank 0 NCCL watchdog timeout traceback. In synchronous distributed training, healthy victim ranks emit collective timeouts becaus…
articles.body: Quick Answer: Never restart a crashed multi-node GPU job solely from a rank 0 NCCL watchdog timeout traceback. In synchronous distributed training, healthy victim ranks emit collective timeouts because they blocked waiting on one silent failing peer. Always screen all allocated hosts for kernel NVRM: Xid events and cgroup OOM kills first, isolate the originating rank via collective sequence timestamps, and drain faulty hardware before rescheduling.

articles.title: Why your friend can't open localhost:8000 (and the 4 things an AI-built app actually needs before sharing)
articles.excerpt: You asked an AI coding agent for an app and it works. The terminal prints http://localhost:8000, the page looks right, so you paste the link to a friend. They get "This site can't be reached." Nothing…
articles.body: You asked an AI coding agent for an app and it works. The terminal prints http://localhost:8000 , the page looks right, so you paste the link to a friend. They get "This site can't be reached." Nothing is broken. localhost is not a place on the internet. It is a name for whichever computer is asking. The short answer localhost:8000 means "port 8000 on this computer". On your laptop that is your dev server. On your friend's laptop it is their own machine, where nothing is listening. (If something is listening there, they will see their own app instead of yours.) To share the app, it has to run somewhere other people can reach: on your machine behind a tunnel, or on a host. A public address is the easy half.

articles.title: Password Recovery Links Versus One Time Codes Across 2 Devices
articles.excerpt: Imagine the page: password recovery completion has fallen below the media site's SLO, while the on-call dashboard still shows recovery requests being accepted. A reader starts on a laptop, opens the e…
articles.body: Imagine the page: password recovery completion has fallen below the media site's SLO, while the on-call dashboard still shows recovery requests being accepted. A reader starts on a laptop, opens the email on a phone, and cannot finish the session-bound link flow. This is a hypothetical alert, but it exposes the decision that matters when adding Google and GitHub social sign-in alongside password accounts: which recovery path can the reader actually complete? Short answer: a reset link takes fewer steps; a one-time code works across devices but adds typing. Both can be safe when the credential is short-lived and single-use. For this media site, choose the default around the reader's device transition, then verify expiry and single use independently of the delivery format.

articles.title: Three people connected our app from Claude's connector directory, and none of them shipped an app: what we fixed
articles.excerpt: We make Tofu, a service that puts apps and websites online from a chat. Tofu has a connector that people can add to Claude, and it was listed in Claude's connector directory from 4 October 2026 as a C…
articles.body: We make Tofu, a service that puts apps and websites online from a chat. Tofu has a connector that people can add to Claude, and it was listed in Claude's connector directory from 4 October 2026 as a Community connector. Between 5 and 21 October, three accounts added it inside Claude, approved the connection on our own page and created an account as part of that approval. When we looked on 23 October, none of them had a project. No app, no deploy, and no later visit that made anything. This post covers what the records showed, what went wrong, what we changed, and what we have not tested yet. The short version Three accounts: one on 5 October, one on 19 October and one on 21 October. Each connected and signed up within the same minute, then stopped. The product worked as built.

articles.title: When do two Korean filenames in a ZIP become one after NFC normalization?
articles.excerpt: A ZIP from a supplier contains two files with names that look identical. Before deleting one or normalizing both names, check whether their full archive paths would match after normalization. Two entr…
articles.body: A ZIP from a supplier contains two files with names that look identical. Before deleting one or normalizing both names, check whether their full archive paths would match after normalization . Two entries in the same folder converged on one name in our test. The same pair in different folders did not. 01 · Why does one name take 19 bytes or 37 bytes? The Korean part of 거래명세서.txt can be represented as precomposed Hangul syllables or as sequences of individual jamo. Unicode normalization gives canonically equivalent text a consistent representation. In this example, NFC uses precomposed syllables and NFD uses decomposed jamo. A renderer can display both forms alike even when software compares different strings.

articles.excerpt: Your guide to December's full Cold Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: Explore Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' Monuments in marble, Ejecta prints, Launch Sequence sculptures and interactive Crowded Sky at Heft Gallery in New York City.
articles.body: When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos.

articles.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
articles.excerpt: The FCC has given SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit, a move that could transform the landscape of the final frontier.
articles.body: Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions.
